name: M270A1 MLRS

placement_rationale.text: M270A1 fires the same GMLRS-family guided rockets as HIMARS and, per this asset's own characteristics, shares a similar range envelope (ER GMLRS to roughly 70 km) — 18 km therefore draws on only about a quarter of that reach, a wide margin consistent with doctrine.md §2's counter-battery survivability logic for the deep-strike layer. The tracked chassis is heavier and slower to displace than a wheeled launcher, so the platform trades some of the fast shoot-and-scoot cycle for a larger onboard magazine (12 rockets vs. HIMARS' 6) and leans on standoff distance rather than displacement speed for survivability. 18 km sits inside doctrine.md's 10–150+ km medium/long-range strike/recon band, outside the close-in 0–10 km FPV strike zone.

characteristics: 12-round GMLRS pod (double HIMARS' magazine), tracked chassis, similar guided-rocket range to HIMARS
Strength: Larger onboard magazine than HIMARS for sustained fire missions before reloading
Limitation: Tracked chassis is slower on roads and more maintenance-intensive than HIMARS' wheeled chassis
Estimated quantity available: Delivered in smaller numbers than HIMARS; exact total not fully disclosed
employment_notes: Provides the same deep-strike guided-rocket capability as HIMARS with greater immediate firepower per launcher, at the cost of mobility
contrast_vs_traditional: MLRS doctrine originally meant massed, unguided rocket barrages against area targets. Fired with GMLRS precision-guided rounds and cued by drone reconnaissance, it does the same job HIMARS does elsewhere on this map — a single ISR-identified target struck in minutes rather than an area saturated on a schedule — the same shift from area to precision fires doctrine.md describes for the whole deep-strike layer.
